column8: The Ruzsa distance between two random variables X and Y that take values in a group G is calculated using the entropy of independent copies of X and Y, specifically as the entropy of their difference minus half the entropy of each variable. This measures how spread out the difference of the variables is, adjusted for their individual randomness. It is always non-negative and equals zero only when X and Y are structurally similar in a specific probabilistic sense. The definition relies on having independent versions of the random variables to compute the difference properly.

This measures a kind of divergence between the distributions of X and Y in an additive group setting.

column8: A log-size ball sequence is a process in a metric space where, starting from a finite set J, points are iteratively removed in balls around selected centers, with radii based on a logarithmic size measure, until no points remain. The sequence tracks the remaining points, chosen centers, and associated radii at each step. The removal radius decreases by a fixed factor c adjusted by the log-size radius minus one. This continues as long as points are left in the set.
column9: \uses{def:logSizeRadius} \mathlibok \lean{PairReduction.logSizeBallSeq} Let $(T,d_T)$ be a metric space and let $J \subseteq T$ be finite, $a,c \in \mathbb R_+$ with $a \ge 1$ and $n \in \{1, 2, ...\}$ such that $|J| \le a^n$. An log-size ball sequence for $(J, a, c, n)$ is a sequence of $(V_i, t_i, r_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ such that \begin{itemize} \item $V_0 = J$, $t_0$ is an arbitrary point in $J$, \item for all $i$, $r_i$ is the log-size radius of $t_i$ in $V_i$, \item $V_{i+1} = V_i \setminus B_{V_i}(t_i, (r_i - 1)c)$, $t_{i+1}$ is arbitrarily chosen in $V_{i+1}$. \end{itemize}
